rules.rule:
Focus on correctness, regression risk, error handling, interface consistency, and missing tests. Distinguish concrete defects from optional improvements.

Apply code-minimality review. Flag when the diff reimplements an existing helper, module, or installed dependency that could be reused; introduces an unnecessary abstraction such as a wrapper, adapter, factory, registry, manager, or service layer; adds a third-party dependency where the standard library or a platform-native capability already suffices; could shrink its change scope; could delete code instead of extending it; or adds YAGNI-style speculative capability. For bug fixes, flag symptom patches (workaround, special case, extra fallback) that leave the root cause unrepaired. Tag these findings with an internal category: delete, reuse, stdlib, native, yagni, shrink, or root-cause. Keep the existing review output format. Code minimality is advisory only: never recommend removing or weakening input validation, error handling, permission or security checks, auditability, accessibility, or deterministic gate behavior, and never accept fewer lines as a reason to cut them.

For added or changed lines, flag any explanatory comment whose absence would not cause a concrete foreseeable mistake, including optional explanations, redundant API prose, commented-out code, and decorative separators (preserve required notices, machine directives, and mandatory external contracts), duplicate or trivial tests, mocks that only assert implementation details, and unnecessary new documentation. Prefer extending existing behavior tests; keep necessary regression, security, integration, and machine-contract tests. Require a concrete retirement condition for temporary compatibility. Do not enforce arbitrary line or test-count ratios. For every comment finding, identify the added comment and the code that already communicates its meaning; do not demand a replacement comment or written justification. For every redundant test finding, identify the existing test or assertion that already detects the same failure, or explain why the asserted behavior cannot regress independently. Do not request a new test file if extending an existing case suffices. Review changed lines only; preserve meaningful tests and necessary comments. Cite the concrete redundancy and a safe alternative; keep findings advisory.
